scope: Exact-crosswalk gate review for the Peten milpa and Roman Palmyra three-day hinterland validation cases.

geometry_and_table_manifest.area_measurement: Current frozen accepted table area_km2 values, summed over explicitly selected location_tag rows; no historical polygon intersection was available.
geometry_and_table_manifest.source_hash_scope: Hashes identify the exact local EU5 area/geometry inputs used for the measured selector totals. Remote article and Zenodo checksums are recorded per crosswalk.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Central Peten study region reported as 35,854 km2 in Schwartz and Corzo (2015); the article describes a 60%-managed milpa system but does not distribute a GIS polygon or machine-readable boundary.

measured_area.area_ratio_interpretation: Sanity-check only. This is not a geometric coverage fraction because the published study boundary is not available as a polygon.

local_food_and_pressure.local_food_support: The source explicitly evaluates traditional local milpa production rather than an imported urban food supply.
local_food_and_pressure.pressure_evidence: The authors frame 3-4 million as a conservative provisionable population under a 60%-managed Peten system; this is a physical carrying-capacity assessment, not an independent dated population census.
local_food_and_pressure.trade_or_urban_caveat: No urban import adjustment is used, but the record remains a modelled capacity analogue and is not a scale anchor.

sources.citation: Schwartz and Corzo (2015), Swidden Counts: A Peten, Guatemala, Milpa System Production, Carrying Capacity, and Sustainability in the Southern Maya Lowlands, Journal of Archaeological Research.
sources.locator: Abstract: 35,854 km2 Peten study region; no downloadable polygon located.
sources.hash_status: article PDF endpoint returned access denial during audit; URL/DOI retained as citation, no local binary hash claimed

crosswalks.resolution_method: Deterministically summed the ten explicit location_tag rows in the frozen accepted table. Because no historical Peten polygon or boundary vertices are distributed by the cited source, a polygon intersection and >=95% coverage calculation cannot be performed.
rejection_reasons: The 7.09% area discrepancy is already greater than the 5% maximum allowed for an exact quantitative crosswalk.
More importantly, area agreement alone cannot establish overlap, containment, or which parts of the study region are represented by the ten centroids.
Do not promote this record to a training target or call the selector exact without obtaining the authors' geospatial boundary.
crosswalks.notes: The existing benchmark TOML's 33,631 km2 figure is stale relative to the frozen accepted table (33,312.73842 km2); this artifact uses the latter and records the discrepancy explicitly. No Peten-, Maya- or Africa-specific multiplier is permitted.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Three-day camel-travel Palmyra catchment reconstructed by travel-cost contours around Palmyra. The paper's 3-day envelope is shown in Fig. 2; Zenodo supplements provide QGIS reproduction instructions but not the resulting contour/polygon files.

measured_area.area_ratio_interpretation: Sanity-check only. The ratio is close to 1 but is not a geometric coverage fraction without the source contour polygon.

local_food_and_pressure.local_food_support: The PLOS ONE model explicitly reconstructs local Palmyra hinterland agriculture and food security; imported caravan food is not treated as intrinsic capacity.
local_food_and_pressure.pressure_evidence: The paper models nine-in-ten-year food security under deteriorating climate and storage/transport losses, with an optimal-year ceiling; this supports physical validation but is not a dated rural Malthusian equilibrium census.
local_food_and_pressure.trade_or_urban_caveat: Palmyra was a caravan city. The catchment is intended as local food support, but the urban/trade context and model-derived interval prevent scale-anchor promotion.

sources.citation: Food security in Roman Palmyra (Syria) in light of paleoclimatological evidence and its historical implications, PLOS ONE 17(8):e0273241.
sources.locator: Methods: three travel-time catchments; Fig. 2: 1-, 3- and 5-day catchment envelopes; Data Availability points to Zenodo supplementary files.
sources.hash_status: URL/DOI citation retained; no local article PDF hash claimed

sources.citation: Supplementary Materials for Food security in Roman Palmyra, Zenodo record 7009590.
sources.locator: S2/S3: reproduce Water_Cost_3 raster, contour 18 and manual Area_Far polygon; no original Area_Far.shp/GeoJSON distributed.

sources.citation: Syrian Desert Water Sources, Seland DataverseNO.
sources.locator: Input water-source dataset referenced by Zenodo S1/S2; original water-source vector was not included in the Zenodo record downloaded for this audit.

crosswalks.resolution_method: Deterministically summed the eight explicit location_tag rows in the frozen accepted table. The Zenodo package was downloaded and hash-verified, then inspected: it contains documents, spreadsheets and notebook/source code, while S2/S3 instruct the user to manually recreate contours and polygons from local rasters. No original three-day polygon is available for EU5 intersection.
rejection_reasons: A near-equal area ratio (96.00%) is not proof of >=95% geometric coverage; the selector could omit or include different land than the historical travel-cost contour.
The original Area_Far/three-day catchment polygon is not distributed in the cited Zenodo record, so mapped and unmapped boundary area cannot be measured.
Keep as held-out physical validation only; do not train or promote to a scale anchor without an archived source contour polygon or a deterministic reconstruction from all original input rasters.
crosswalks.notes: The existing benchmark TOML's 25,674 km2 figure is stale relative to the frozen accepted table (24,430.37628 km2); this artifact uses the latter and retains the 25,447 km2 published three-day sanity-check area.

disposition.required_follow_up: Obtain an author-archived Peten study polygon and Palmyra Area_Far/three-day travel-cost polygon plus all input rasters, then rerun polygon intersection against the frozen EU5 geometry. Until then, coverage_fraction remains null and neither record can supervise training.
